full_judgment: In the Supreme Court case 6 DLR (SC) 61 relied on by the learned Advocate for the appellant, the insurer instituted the suit on the plea that the insurer assigned the policy on the insurer. No objection was taken as there was no appearance on behalf of the defendant and accordingly the suit was decreed ex parte. In the Supreme Court it was pleaded that in the absence of any written instrument of assignment the plaintiff was not entitled to institute the suit and secondly, that in view of the provision of section 135A of the Transfer of Property Act the insurer being subrogated in place of the insured could sue. As regards that first ground, it was observed that the procedural law of Pakistan did not countenance the failure of a suit for mere misjoinder or on nonjoinder of the parties; that it was the law that objection on this ground would not be entertained unless it was taken at the earliest possible opportunity and as the same was not taken at the earliest possible opportunity that contention could not been entertained. As to the subrogation under section 135A of the Transfer of Property Act, it was observed that as the insurer on payment was subrogated in place of the assured the suit at the instance of the insurer was maintainable.
